summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil-recruitment axis: the receptor CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking, followed by CXCR1 and their ligand CXCL8, all raised in the same direction in all eight biopsy cohorts. CXCR2 is the only one of the three that combines robust expression with genetic association and clinical-stage small-molecule antagonists. Single-cell, composition and in-situ data agree, however, that these transcripts come almost entirely from infiltrating neutrophils, and that their response association in the ustekinumab trial is mirrored in placebo non-responders. The axis is therefore best read as a strong marker of neutrophilic activity and a target acting on arriving cells, not as a change of resident tissue.

Changes that survive composition adjustment and replicate across single-cell datasets and in situ point to resident cells: MMP1 and CHI3L1 in inflammatory fibroblasts, DUOX2 in epithelium and IDO1 in myeloid or epithelial cells. These are the most credible tissue-level candidates. MMP inhibitors carry a history of toxicity, CHI3L1 and DUOX2 have no drug, and none of them has genetic support, so they are stronger biomarkers and mechanistic leads than validated targets. The mirror image is the loss of the mature colonocyte programme (AQP8, CLDN8, HMGCS2, SLC26A2), which is local to inflamed mucosa and marks epithelial state rather than a druggable lesion.

Genetics separates the candidates sharply. Known UC targets act as positive controls: IL12B is the strongest plasma Mendelian randomisation hit with colocalisation, and JAK2 has one of the highest Open Targets association scores despite a modest transcript change. In contrast, the plasma MR for CD274 (PD-L1) and CXCL5 points in the protective direction, so blocking them would be expected to be unfavourable, while CXCL8, IDO1, IL2RA and FCGR2A have null plasma MR. Biopsy expression and causal genetics therefore largely identify different genes.

Pathway activity (JAK-STAT, TNFa, NFkB, TGFb and STAT3) is raised in every cohort but is non-specific and mostly already drugged. Baseline biopsy associations with non-response to ustekinumab (OSM, TREM1, IL11, CXCR2, TNFa) are mirrored in UNIFI placebo non-responders and have null drug-vs-placebo interactions, so they track disease severity rather than drug-specific resistance. The drug targets' own transcripts (IL23A for ustekinumab, ITGB7 for vedolizumab) do not separate responders.

expression.text: Across the random-effects meta-analysis of eight biopsy cohorts, CXCL8 is one of the most significant and reproducible increases, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864] and BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.54e-29], significantly up in every cohort. As the main ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, it anchors the neutrophil-recruitment module (with CXCL1 and CXCL5) that dominates the top of the convergence ranking.

The largest increases are antimicrobial, neutrophil and tissue-remodelling genes. CHI3L1 rises by pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875], the calprotectin subunit S100A8 by [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77], MMP3 by [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901] (with MMP1, MMP7 and MMP10 following), the epithelial oxidase DUOX2 by [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412] and the interferon-induced tryptophan catabolic enzyme IDO1 by [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118], all in the same direction in all eight cohorts. By contrast, the genetically supported JAK2 changes only modestly, pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874], so its standing rests on genetics and drugs rather than on transcript level.

The strongest losses describe a mature colonocyte losing its absorptive and metabolic programme. AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss, log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246], significantly down in seven of eight cohorts; the tight-junction gene CLDN8 falls by [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.291] and the ketogenic enzyme HMGCS2, which supplies butyrate-derived energy to colonocytes, by [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]. With SLC26A2, PCK1 and the guanylin genes these are markers of epithelial state rather than targets.

inflammation.text: In the paired MSCCR contrast (inflamed vs non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient), most leading changes are local to inflamed tissue. CXCR2 rises by [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972], CXCL8 by [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.968], CHI3L1 by [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.618] and MMP7 by [gene=MMP7; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.88], while the epithelial genes HMGCS2 and CLDN8 fall by [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.951] and [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.97]. These track active inflammation within a patient.

Only a few changes are already present in non-inflamed mucosa compared with controls. DUOX2 is modestly raised there, log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8129], suggesting some disease-intrinsic epithelial activation, and CXCR2 shows a smaller rise of [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. HMGCS2 is essentially unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa, [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649] and not significant, so the loss of epithelial metabolism is a consequence of active inflammation rather than a pre-existing trait.

replication.text: The discovery cohort (MSCCR, RNA-seq) reproduces well in the four microarray cohorts (UNIFI, PURSUIT-SC and the two Leuven cohorts) and the three RNA-seq cohorts (PROTECT, RISK and an adult colon series). CXCL8 is up in the discovery cohort by [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=2.2841] and significantly up in all seven replication cohorts, reaching [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=7.205] in the Leuven infliximab cohort; HMGCS2 falls by [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-2.1465] in discovery and is significantly down in every replication cohort. Direction replicates almost perfectly for the top-ranked genes, but magnitude does not: between-cohort heterogeneity is high (for CHI3L1, I2 [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.918]) because platforms, disease extent and patient age differ, so direction and significance are more informative than pooled size.

literature.text: Published support for the leading candidates is mostly mechanistic and preclinical. The literature places the CXCL8 axis with its receptors CXCR1 and CXCR2 in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling and lists CXCL8 as a protein-interaction hub gene; IDO1 is reported to drive pro-inflammatory macrophage polarisation through ER stress, with an IDO inhibitor ameliorating DSS colitis; CHI3L1 is linked to inflammasome activity and macrophage pyroptosis; and AQP9 is described as a neutrophil gene that promotes NET formation and epithelial injury in colitis models. Each rests on few studies, mostly single preclinical reports, and no clinical trial in UC appears among the extracted relations for any top-ranked gene. CXCR2 itself, the top-ranked gene, has no extracted literature relation in this corpus; its literature component comes only from Open Targets and from the CXCL8 axis.

The biomarker literature is more consistent than the target literature. MMP10 is reported up in active versus remission UC and even in preclinical UC before diagnosis; S100A9 performs well for diagnosing active UC and falls in resident macrophages with tofacitinib response; reduced SLC26A2 correlates with Mayo score and PUCAI; DUOX2 is among the most elevated proteins in inflamed biopsies; and MMP1, MMP3, S100A8 and IL1B transcripts changed by mirikizumab correlate with histological indices. Several reported accuracy figures concern IBD as a whole or UC-associated colorectal cancer (MMP1, LCN2) rather than UC alone, and CXCL1 shows only modest single-gene accuracy.

external.text: Approved and clinical UC targets behave as positive controls. IL12B is the top known UC target in Open Targets (association score [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7424]) and the strongest plasma-protein Mendelian randomisation hit, with higher protein raising UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]) and colocalisation, consistent with IL-12 and IL-23 blockade by ustekinumab. JAK2 has an association score of [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318] and JAK inhibitors are in use, though its transcript barely changes. The expression-led candidates differ: CXCR2 (association score [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345]) has antagonists in trials for other indications but no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR is untested; CHI3L1, DUOX2, AQP9 and MMP10 have no drug and no genetic association, and SLC26A3 is a genetically associated epithelial transporter that is lost rather than inhibitable.

Genetic direction argues against blocking two up-regulated genes. For CD274 (PD-L1), higher plasma protein lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]) with colocalisation to an IBD GWAS signal, so its biopsy rise looks like protective feedback and PD-L1 blockade would be expected to be unfavourable. CXCL5 shows the same protective direction (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]) but via a tag variant without colocalisation. Plasma MR is null for CXCL8 (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]), IDO1 (p [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]), IL2RA (p [gene=IL2RA; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.237]) and FCGR2A (p [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.68]); for IDO1 and IL2RA the colon eQTL MR is also not significant, so blood and gut agree on the absence of causal support. The strongest gut eQTL hits (IRF8, IRF5, GSDMA and GSDMB) are not among the top expression-ranked genes.

cells.text: CXCR2, the top-ranked candidate, is almost entirely a neutrophil transcript in inflamed mucosa (Gubatan neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]). In Smillie, which captured no neutrophils, the residual signal falls in T/NK and macrophage clusters and the second dataset says myeloid, so the lineage attribution does not replicate. In situ settles it: neutrophils explain CXCR2 in deconvolved Visium spots and lead the Xenium attribution in inflamed sections. After composition adjustment only part of the change remains, [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. A CXCR2 antagonist would act on arriving neutrophils, not on resident tissue cells.

The other neutrophil and myeloid genes behave the same way, which separates markers of inflammation from targets in a cell type. Neutrophils carry most CXCL8 transcripts in Gubatan ([gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]) and its composition-adjusted change is no longer significant (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]); IL1B likewise loses significance (adjusted padj [gene=IL1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0728]). S100A8 (neutrophil share [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]) and AQP9 (neutrophil share [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]) keep a smaller positive adjusted change, and CXCR1 and CXCL1 behave as influx markers with a minor tissue component. The adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so a lost change is not proof of pure influx.

Resident-cell changes survive adjustment and replicate. MMP1 is made chiefly by inflammatory fibroblasts (stromal share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]) and keeps an adjusted change of [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]; CHI3L1 sits in inflammatory fibroblasts (share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941], adjusted [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]); DUOX2 is epithelial (share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], adjusted [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]); and IDO1 is myeloid with an epithelial contribution and little neutrophil input (share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]). MMP10 retains the largest adjusted change among the genes checked ([gene=MMP10; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.5838]). For MMP1, CHI3L1 and DUOX2 the cell attribution replicates in the second dataset and in Visium spots; CD274 is diffuse across plasma cells, macrophages, enterocytes and neutrophils, with no clear cell type to target.

spatial.text: In deconvolved Visium spots most leading candidates map to the cell groups that single-cell data assigned them. Neutrophils explain CXCR2 ([gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.386]) and are the only cell group enriched around its high spots, and they explain S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.632]); inflammatory fibroblasts explain MMP1 ([gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]), with fibroblasts and neutrophils around its high spots; and epithelial cells explain DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.812]), the cleanest agreement, confirmed in Xenium single cells where expressing cells are surrounded by epithelium. For CXCR2 the in-situ view resolves the single-cell disagreement in favour of neutrophils.

Tissue and single cells disagree for some genes. CXCL8 is mainly neutrophil in spots ([gene=CXCL8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.609]) but also draws on inflammatory fibroblasts, a contribution not seen at single-cell level. For CHI3L1 the largest raw contributor is plasma cells ([gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.258]), and only the composition-corrected source and the enriched neighbours point to inflammatory fibroblasts. IDO1 is ambiguous: epithelium has the largest raw share ([gene=IDO1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.349]) and leads in Xenium, while the corrected source is myeloid. CD274 has no clear in-situ source ([gene=CD274; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.234]) and no enriched neighbours. Visium spots hold several cells and few UC sections express each gene, so this is moderate evidence.

pathways.text: Inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once. JAK-STAT activity is up in every cohort [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=8], and TNFa is likewise up in every cohort, with NFkB, EGFR, Hypoxia, MAPK, PI3K and TGFb following. Inferred STAT3 transcription-factor activity is up in all eight cohorts, strongest in MSCCR [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6], but AP1, CEBPD and ATF factors are equally replicated. These axes are robust but generic and largely already drugged (JAK inhibitors, anti-TNF). As a negative result, the Androgen pathway is inconsistent, up in only a minority of cohorts [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=2].

The most specific cell-cell circuit is neutrophil-centred. In the Gubatan single-cell data, CXCL8 from neutrophil states (CXCR4-high and OSM-high neutrophils) is co-expressed with CXCR2 on other neutrophil states, a recruitment loop that increases in inflamed mucosa [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755], and neutrophil CXCL8 also reaches ACKR1 on venular endothelium, a leukocyte-trafficking site [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.991]. This is the untargeted-in-UC CXCR2 axis, with antagonists only in other indications. IL1B from macrophages and neutrophils pairs with IL1R2 on neutrophils [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.059], but IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this may be a brake rather than activation. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

Not every proposed circuit holds. The neutrophil OSM to IL6ST route on lamina propria fibroblasts is weak and does not increase in inflamed mucosa [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709], and a new neutrophil PADI4 pair has a low score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=86.523], so an OSM-driven neutrophil-to-fibroblast circuit is not supported here even though OSM is up in tissue. Among untargeted axes, CHI3L1 stands out as a strongly increased fibroblast product with no drug, but no ligand-receptor partner was resolved for it.

treatment.text: Pathway activity at baseline is associated with non-response, but mostly as a severity signal. TNFa activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=4.79]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), though not in PURSUIT placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]). JAK-STAT is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab non-response but not vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]); TGFb is associated in ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but not golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]), with UNIFI placebo also significant.

At gene level, baseline OSM (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), TREM1 ([gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]), IL11 ([gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]) and CXCR2 ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) are higher in ustekinumab non-responders. Yet TREM1 (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), IL11 ([gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]) and CXCR2 ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]) are also higher in UNIFI placebo non-responders; OSM trends the same way in placebo ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]) and its drug-vs-placebo interaction is null ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]). These are severity markers, not drug-specific resistance signals. The drug targets themselves do not predict response: IL23A for ustekinumab ([gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and ITGB7 for vedolizumab ([gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), and CXCL8 is not significant in golimumab ([gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]).

discovery.text: CHRDL2 is the top first-in-class candidate of the discovery screen. It is made mostly by stromal cells, chiefly inflammatory fibroblasts (lineage share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939]), but only a minority of its bulk increase survives composition correction (retained fraction [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.276]), so much of the signal reflects fibroblast expansion. Its highest vital-organ RNA, [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM, is a safety flag. Tractability is predicted only; genetic support, functional data and any response association are missing. It is a hypothesis for validation in fibroblast models.

XKR9 is the only top discovery candidate classified as intrinsic to the tissue: it is epithelial, and most of its increase is retained after composition correction (retained fraction [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.798]). That makes it the cleanest tissue-level hypothesis, but it is up in only a few cohorts and few cells express it, so both replication and cellular evidence are weak. Genetics, tractability and safety have not been established.

LAX1 comes mainly from plasma cells in inflamed mucosa (transcript share [gene=LAX1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.433]), and the lineage does not replicate cleanly between datasets. Its retained fraction after composition correction is low ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.230]), so it most likely marks plasma-cell infiltration rather than a tissue change. Vital-organ RNA is low, which is favourable for safety, but without replication of the cell source it remains a weak, exploratory candidate.

integration.text: The streams agree most where expression, replication, cell source and in-situ data line up on a single cell type. The CXCR2 and CXCL8 neutrophil axis is consistent across all eight cohorts, the paired inflamed contrast, single-cell attribution with neutrophils, Visium deconvolution and ligand-receptor analysis, and CXCR2 also has genetic association and clinical antagonists, which is why it ranks first. Fibroblast MMP1 and CHI3L1 and epithelial DUOX2 are consistent across expression, composition adjustment, two single-cell datasets and in-situ maps, and are backed by preclinical or biomarker literature, which makes them the most credible tissue-level candidates.

They disagree on three points. First, expression and genetics pick different genes: the most strongly changed transcripts (CXCL8, CHI3L1, DUOX2, MMPs) have no genetic association, while genetically supported genes (IL12B, JAK2, FCGR2A, IL2RA) change little in bulk tissue. Second, genetics contradicts a naive reading of expression for CD274 and CXCL5, whose plasma MR points in the protective direction even though both are up in inflamed mucosa. Third, the clinical response data do not single out any drug-specific mechanism: the genes and pathways that separate non-responders do so in placebo arms too, so convergence in this analysis identifies disease activity markers and candidate mechanisms rather than predictors of drug response.

targets.rationale: Ranks first by convergence: up in all eight cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa, genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists in other indications. Single-cell and Visium data place it on infiltrating neutrophils, and its response association is mirrored in placebo, so it is a target acting on recruited cells and a strong neutrophil-activity marker rather than a resident-tissue lesion.

Positive control: not in the expression-led top 25, but the top known UC target in Open Targets and the strongest plasma MR hit with colocalisation, supporting the approved IL-12 and IL-23 blockade. Placed above expression-led genes because causal genetics is the most direct support for a target.

Positive control for an approved mechanism (JAK inhibition): high Open Targets genetic association and JAK-STAT activity up in every cohort, despite only a modest transcript change, which shows that bulk expression underrates genetically supported signalling targets.

Ranks third and is one of the most significant, perfectly replicated increases, but has no genetic association, null plasma MR, loses significance after composition adjustment and anti-CXCL8 antibodies stopped at mid-stage trials. Best used as a neutrophil-activity biomarker; its receptor CXCR2 is the better drug entry point.

Among the largest replicated increases, with a strong composition-retained change from inflammatory fibroblasts confirmed in a second dataset and after correction in Visium, preclinical literature on inflammasome and pyroptosis, and no drug. Raised above its numeric rank because it is a resident-cell change; lacks genetic support.

A fibroblast-derived tissue change that survives composition adjustment and is confirmed in situ, with histology-correlated biomarker literature. Broad MMP inhibitors have a toxicity history and there is no genetic support, so selective inhibition or use as an activity marker is more realistic than repurposing.

The cleanest epithelial-intrinsic change: epithelial in both single-cell datasets, Visium and Xenium, retained after adjustment and already raised in non-inflamed mucosa. No drug and no genetic support, so it is a mechanism and biomarker lead.

Strong, replicated increase that does not depend on neutrophil influx, with clinical-stage inhibitors from oncology and preclinical colitis data. Plasma and colon eQTL MR are null and the in-situ cell source is ambiguous, which keeps it below the resident-cell candidates.

Up in all eight cohorts with genetic association, but plasma MR with colocalisation shows higher PD-L1 lowers UC risk. It is a protective-feedback signal: blockade (approved in oncology) would be unfavourable, and agonism is the direction of interest. Kept in the list as a genetics-guided warning rather than a blocking target.
Calprotectin subunit with one of the largest replicated increases, made by neutrophils in single-cell and Visium data; an established inflammatory-burden marker rather than a target.
Retains the largest adjusted change among the genes checked and has the most consistent biomarker literature among MMPs, including elevation before diagnosis.

Marks loss of epithelial ketogenesis: down in all eight cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa and unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa, so it is a marker of active inflammation and mucosal healing, not a target.

Exploratory: top first-in-class candidate, made by inflammatory fibroblasts, but mostly a composition signal with a vital-organ expression flag and no genetic or functional support; a hypothesis for experimental validation.

Exploratory: the only discovery candidate classified as tissue-intrinsic (epithelial, mostly retained after composition correction), but weakly replicated across cohorts and expressed by few cells; a hypothesis for experimental validation.

limitations.text: Bulk biopsy increases in immune genes mix cell influx and activation; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so a change lost after adjustment is not proof of pure influx.

Only the MSCCR cohort has a paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast; the other cohorts compare UC with controls and mix disease extent, age and platform, which produces high between-cohort heterogeneity in effect size.

Smillie did not capture neutrophils, so neutrophil genes are attributed to other cell types there; Visium spots hold several cells, few UC sections express each gene, and many candidates (CXCL8, MMP1, CHI3L1, S100A8, CD274) are not on the Xenium panel.

Plasma MR is not tissue MR, and many leading candidates (CXCR2, JAK2) have no cis instrument, which is not evidence against them; Open Targets drug lists include trials in other indications, and none of the expression-led candidates has been tested in UC here.

Ligand-receptor results are co-expression in a single neutrophil-containing dataset, not proof of signalling; the integrin (vedolizumab) and IL-23 axes were not queried individually in the communication analysis.

Treatment-response analyses are baseline associations; the infliximab and vedolizumab arms are small, the ustekinumab arm is much larger and therefore better powered, and no drug-vs-placebo interaction was significant for the genes checked.

The literature relations are mostly single preclinical or bioinformatic studies, and many top-ranked genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CD274, FCGR2A, JAK2) have no extracted relation, so their literature component rests on Open Targets alone.

CPXM1, a stromal discovery candidate in both single-cell datasets, is not included among the targets because only a minority of its increase survives composition adjustment and it lacks genetic, functional and response support.
